hypothesis: The wirelength model's gamma schedule is the single strongest lever on how tightly cells cluster (small gamma = HPWL-like, strong pull; large gamma = diffuse). Making the overflow→gamma coefficient less aggressive at low overflow keeps the model closer to HPWL early (denser, shorter critical nets) and only diffuses when congestion is really high, which should shorten many moderate paths and reduce TNS on all circuits.
analysis: Hypothesis partly failed: total score −0.030, robust −0.074, with 2 of 3 cases worse. Ariane133-ng45 (dTNS −9.2%) and bp-ng45 (dWNS −7.0%) regressed, while bp_fe-ng45 improved (+13.8% WNS, +4.3% TNS). Mechanism: keeping gamma HPWL-like early densifies cells, but at overflow ~111–139 this likely over-congests moderate paths, hurting TNS; only the higher-overflow case (165) benefited from delayed diffusion. Next step: make the overflow→gamma coefficient overflow-adaptive with a threshold near 150, so densification persists only below it, and re-test across seeds.
